questions.question: In C/C++, when passing an argument by value to a function, what actually happens to the variable in the caller function?
options: Variable a becomes 6 because x is modified
Variable a remains 5 because a copy of the value is passed
A compile-time error occurs due to parameter mismatch
Variable a becomes 0 due to stack cleanup
questions.explanation: In pass-by-value, a separate copy of the parameter is allocated on the stack. Changes made inside increment() do not affect variable a in main().

questions.question: Which syntax correctly defines a function that modifies the original integer in the caller via pointer passing in C?
questions.explanation: Using int *num receives the memory address. Dereferencing with *num = ... mutates the memory cell at caller location.

questions.question: What is the base case condition required to prevent infinite recursion in this countdown function?
questions.explanation: if (n <= 0) return; or if (n == 0) return; terminates recursion once zero is reached, avoiding stack overflow.

questions.question: In a 0-indexed array of size N (e.g., int arr[10]), what is the valid index range for elements?
questions.explanation: For size N, valid indices are always 0 through N - 1. Accessing arr[10] causes an off-by-one buffer overrun error.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in an array by its index, e.g. arr[i]?
questions.explanation: Arrays allocate contiguous memory blocks. The address is calculated instantly via baseAddress + i * sizeof(type), yielding O(1) random access.

questions.question: Which of the following data types in C typically occupies 4 bytes of memory on a 64-bit architecture?
questions.explanation: Standard `int` is 4 bytes (32 bits), `char` is 1 byte, `double` is 8 bytes, and `short` is 2 bytes.

questions.question: What will be the output of a for loop running from i = 0 while i < 5 with i++?
questions.explanation: It iterates through values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, which is exactly 5 iterations.

questions.question: Which mechanism is required in C to pass an array to a function?
options: Passed by copy of all elements
Passed by pointer to first element (base address)
Passed by reference automatically as in Python
Cannot pass arrays to functions in C
questions.explanation: Arrays decay to a pointer to their first element when passed as function arguments.

mistake_logs.errorPattern: Repeated mistake: Confusing pass-by-value with pass-by-reference in C.
mistake_logs.rootCause: Assuming modifying a local parameter mutates the original variable in caller.
mistake_logs.sampleSnippet: void swap(int a, int b) { int t = a; a = b; b = t; }
mistake_logs.recommendedPractice: Practice 5 parameter-passing problems before moving forward.

mistake_logs.errorPattern: Nested loop variable shadowing / incorrect loop bounds.
mistake_logs.rootCause: Reusing counter variable or missing boundary decrement.
mistake_logs.sampleSnippet: for(int i=0; i<N; i++) { for(int i=0; i<M; i++) ... }

mistake_logs.errorPattern: Off-by-one indexing error accessing arr[N] on array of size N.
mistake_logs.rootCause: Index boundary confusion between 1-based size and 0-based index.
mistake_logs.sampleSnippet: int arr[5]; arr[5] = 10; // Out of bounds!
